catalysts.headline: Iran-U.S. Deal Reopens Hormuz Strait, Oil Sanctions Relief Imminent
catalysts.analysis: Trump confirmed the Strait of Hormuz would reopen upon deal signing, signaling a major geopolitical de-escalation in the Middle East. Markets are pricing in reduced supply-disruption risk, which explains today's sharp 3.2% crude oil drop despite rising equities. Watch for formal deal confirmation, Senate ratification signals, and Iran's compliance timeline — any breakdown would spike crude and VIX sharply.

catalysts.headline: WTI Crude -3.28% Despite Risk-On Rally Signals Demand Skepticism
catalysts.analysis: Oil falling sharply while equities surge is an unusual divergence that often signals either demand growth concerns or supply-side shock absorption. The Iran deal prospect floods the market with anticipated supply just as global PMI data remains mixed, creating a deflationary commodity impulse. Watch refiner margins, energy sector earnings guidance, and whether OPEC+ counters with output cuts.

catalysts.headline: Gold +3.55% and Silver +5.23% Surge Simultaneously With Equities — Stagflation Hedge in Play
catalysts.analysis: Precious metals rallying hard alongside equities suggests investors are simultaneously buying growth AND hedging inflation/currency debasement risk. The DXY weakness (-0.13%) and elevated 30Y yield (4.95%) support the thesis that real rates may be peaking, boosting gold's appeal. Watch the gold/10Y real yield inverse correlation and whether $4,300 becomes the next resistance for gold.

catalysts.headline: SpaceX IPO Signals Emerging — Shotwell Addresses Investors
catalysts.analysis: Gwynne Shotwell's exclusive CNBC appearance marks a meaningful shift in SpaceX's public market posture after years of IPO resistance. A SpaceX listing would be the largest tech IPO in history, potentially reshaping index composition and drawing enormous capital flows into space/defense tech. Watch for any formal S-1 filing, valuation leaks (last private round ~$350B), and competitor reactions from Boeing/Northrop.

catalysts.headline: J&J $1B Cancer Bet Reinforces Big Pharma's Oncology Arms Race
catalysts.analysis: Johnson & Johnson committing $1 billion to hard-to-treat cancers signals conviction in precision oncology pipelines even in a high-rate environment. This follows a pattern of mega-cap pharma deploying cash into high-margin therapeutic areas to offset biosimilar pressure on legacy drugs. Watch FDA pipeline decisions, partnership/acquisition targets in the oncology space, and competitor responses from Pfizer, Merck, and AbbVie.

trade_ideas.thesis: $1B oncology investment confirms long-term pipeline conviction with a company trading below its 5-year average P/E; dividend growth and defensive characteristics suit a mixed risk environment.
Gold's 3.55% surge with DXY weakness and real yield pressure creates a technically confirmed breakout — Newmont as gold equity amplifier offers leveraged upside to spot prices.
Iran deal + anticipated supply surge creates a structural headwind for integrated oil majors; Exxon's valuation assumes $80+ sustained WTI which is now at risk.

daily_conclusion:
RESUMEN:
Today was a strong broad-based rally driven by one dominant theme: the proposed Iran-U.S. deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Stocks surged globally, oil crashed, gold hit new highs, and bond yields fell — a rare combination that tells us markets are simultaneously celebrating geopolitical peace AND hedging against the uncertainty of whether this deal will actually hold.
LO MÁS IMPORTANTE:
• Iran-U.S. Hormuz deal — it's the single biggest catalyst today, directly causing oil's 3% crash and powering the global equity rally by reducing war risk premiums
• Gold at $4,235 (+3.55%) rising alongside stocks — this is unusual and signals smart money is hedging against the deal falling apart or inflation staying sticky even if peace holds
• USD/JPY at 160.12 — the Japanese yen is dangerously weak and if Japan's central bank intervenes suddenly to strengthen it, global markets could experience a sharp shock because trillions of dollars of "carry trades" depend on yen staying weak
CONCEPTO DEL DÍA:
Today's concept is **Geopolitical Risk Premium** — the extra price investors demand (or pay) because of uncertainty caused by wars, sanctions, or political instability. Think of it like paying extra for car insurance when you live in a high-accident neighborhood. When the Iran deal was announced, the geopolitical risk premium in oil prices collapsed, which is why crude fell 3% even though everything else was going up — the "insurance cost" was suddenly removed from oil prices.
PARA MAÑANA:
Watch for any official confirmation or denial of the Iran deal signing over the weekend — if Trump or Iranian officials walk back the agreement, Monday's open could see oil spike and equities gap lower sharply. Also monitor any BOJ statements on the yen, as USD/JPY at 160 is historically the level where Japanese authorities have previously intervened.
